relations.subject: sgw:sync-gateway-instance
relations.evidence: Sync Gateway does not support non-default durability settings at the bucket level for [durable writes](../../../server/current/learn/data/durability.md).

relations.subject: sgw:sync-gateway-instance
relations.evidence: You can still use high durability settings when set on the client side.

relations.subject: data:max-ttl-setting
relations.evidence: Document TTL is an Enterprise Edition only feature.

relations.subject: sgw:sync-gateway-instance
relations.evidence: Sync Gateway does not support Bucket-level TTL, make sure your buckets have their `maxTTL` setting set to `0`.

relations.subject: sgw:sync-function
relations.evidence: You can use per-collection sync functions to set expiry on all documents within a collection when you need TTL-like behavior at the collection level, while preserving Sync Gateway's system documents.

notable_absence.finding: The page states that Sync Gateway RETURNS AN ERROR if a bucket's maxTTL is left non-zero ('Sync Gateway returns an error prompting you to set the value to 0 in the Couchbase Server Admin UI') - a specific runtime enforcement behaviour beyond simple non-support, which the doesNotSupport relation above only partially captures. No predicate distinguishes 'silently doesn't work' from 'actively errors out' as behaviours.

cross_component_finding: Collection-level TTL is called out as actively dangerous rather than merely unsupported: 'If these system documents expire due to collection-level TTL, Sync Gateway may malfunction or fail to operate properly' - a stronger and more specific warning than the bucket-level TTL prohibition on the same page, naming a concrete failure mode (loss of `_sync`-prefixed system documents) rather than just a configuration constraint.
